issues.response: Confirmed, and you were right not to ignore the workspace filter or ask for Reception. The pharmacists hold finance.shift.operate, but the Pharmacy workspace (their only one) did not name My cash shift in also_uses, so GET /meta/handbook?workspace=pharmacy left it out, although the pharmacy's cash needs that drawer (report #24: their own shift at the Pharmacy Counter). From fixed_in on (compare overview's server_build with fixed_in): GET /meta/workspaces shows pharmacy also_uses ["my_cash_shift"]. GET /meta/handbook (unscoped and ?workspace=pharmacy) lists my_cash_shift inside Pharmacy Counter, its workspace still naming its home (reception), page screens/my_cash_shift, with the pharmacist's tasks: POST /finance/cash-shifts/open, GET /finance/cash-shifts/mine, GET /finance/cash-shifts/{shift_id}/transactions and POST /finance/cash-shifts/{shift_id}/close. No permission changed, and workspace=reception stays FORBIDDEN for the pharmacist. A test now checks that every role holding finance.shift.operate (cashier, receptionist, pharmacist) finds My cash shift in its own workspace. The screen has a new rule for the Pharmacy workspace (a new checklist item): the drawer must be the Pharmacy Counter's. On a PC whose GET /terminals/whoami cash_node is not PharmacyCounter, say that this PC is not set up for pharmacy cash and that IT must map it to the Pharmacy Counter; never let the user pick the counter. Then: refresh GET /meta/workspaces and GET /meta/handbook?workspace=pharmacy, add My cash shift to the Pharmacy navigation from that answer, and write its F1 page for the pharmacist's tasks and the Pharmacy FAQ entry. Re-read get_screen_bundle('my_cash_shift') (pharmacist is in roles.page_for) and get_ui_quality_brief(workspace='pharmacy'). Frontend guide 17's Pharmacy Counter section now has the reviewer open the shift on a PC mapped to the Pharmacy Counter, sell for cash and by card, read the drawer's expected cash and close it with the counted cash; its write list includes opening and closing the shift. The clinical-and-prescriptions playbook (The pharmacy's cash drawer), the finance-and-owner playbook and guide 12 say the same.

Thank you for keeping the refusal visible without changing terminal 4 or borrowing a shift. The restriction is intended but was documented nowhere. The owner has decided (decisions 51) that the pharmacy's cash stays at the Pharmacy Counter: cash for dispensing (payment_mode Cash) or an OTC sale (method Cash) goes only into the pharmacist's own open shift with node PharmacyCounter, never into a drawer the same person has open at another counter. Card and the other payment modes need no shift. Your shift 10 at MainReception was rightly not used: nothing was sold, no stock moved and that drawer was not touched. From fixed_in on (compare overview's server_build with fixed_in): (1) POST /otc-sales and POST /prescriptions/{prescription_id}/dispense document this, and the refusal says what to do: SHIFT_NOT_OPEN (409, nothing sold) with details.node "PharmacyCounter" and details.open_shift. open_shift is null when the pharmacist has no drawer open, otherwise {shift_id, node} of their own drawer at another counter (yours: {"shift_id": 10, "node": "MainReception"}). So you can say "Your drawer is open at Main Reception; the pharmacy's cash needs your Pharmacy Counter drawer". (2) Check before collecting: GET /finance/cash-shifts/mine?node=PharmacyCounter returns the pharmacist's open shift at the Pharmacy Counter, or null. node takes the cash-node values; without it the call still returns the latest open shift at any counter, which does not count for the pharmacy. The OTC and Dispense screens list that call with a new UX rule (new checklist items): read it before offering Cash; null means Cash is unavailable, with a link to My cash shift, and Card still works. (3) Where the drawer is opened: My cash shift still takes the node from GET /terminals/whoami cash_node. A new rule: in the Pharmacy workspace, on a PC whose cash_node is not PharmacyCounter, say that this PC is not set up for pharmacy cash and that IT must map it to the Pharmacy Counter; never let the user pick the counter. IT maps every PC where the pharmacy takes cash to PharmacyCounter: a new rule on Super Admin (IT), and the hospital IT server guide. A PC the reception and the pharmacy share is mapped PharmacyCounter too, and the reception's cash may then go into that drawer. Opening the drawer from the Pharmacy workspace is the answer to report #25. For your DEV tests, terminal 4 stays MainReception as you asked: to test pharmacy cash, ask the backend team to map a pharmacy test terminal to PharmacyCounter, then open the pharmacist's shift on it. Re-read get_screen_bundle('otc'), get_screen_bundle('dispense') and get_endpoint for POST /otc-sales and GET /finance/cash-shifts/mine. The clinical-and-prescriptions playbook has a new section, The pharmacy's cash drawer. Frontend guide 17's Pharmacy Counter review now opens and closes the shift, sells for cash and by card, and expects this refusal. Your synthetic shift 10 is unaffected: close it as you planned.

Confirmed, and right to keep the clearance disabled rather than guess. GET /admissions/{admission_id}/discharge-status now accepts ipd.admission.view or any stage's clearance permission (ipd.discharge.clear_pharmacy, clear_nursing, clear_billing, clear_cleaning; x-permissions-mode any). Its answer is DischargeStatusViewOut: admission_id, admission_number, patient_id, mrn, patient_name and the admission's status, plus stages (each with status, cleared_by_name and cleared_at), blocked_on, started and complete as before; no clinical detail and no invoice. Every successful read writes phi_access_log. GET /admissions/{admission_id} stays FORBIDDEN without ipd.admission.view. An unknown admission now answers NOT_FOUND (it used to look like a discharge not started); before the doctor's clinical discharge, started is false and stages is empty. The clear call's write_semantics.reconcile_with now names this read (OpenAPI x-reconcile-with) instead of the admission you cannot read, and the dispense screen lists it with a new UX rule (a new checklist item). From fixed_in on (compare overview's server_build with fixed_in): regenerate the type (get_schema('DischargeStatusViewOut'), or generate_typescript for GET /admissions/{admission_id}/discharge-status) and re-read get_screen_bundle('dispense'). Show patient_name, mrn and admission_number and offer the clearance only while blocked_on is PharmacyClearance. After a lost answer of POST /admissions/{admission_id}/discharge/PharmacyClearance/clear, GET discharge-status again: the PharmacyClearance stage Cleared, with cleared_by_name and cleared_at, is the result even when blocked_on has moved on; still Pending means it did not happen, and the pharmacist may press Clear again (a stage already cleared refuses a repeat with DISCHARGE_STAGE_IMMUTABLE, so it is never cleared twice). Never retry automatically. The playbooks inpatient-and-discharge and clinical-and-prescriptions describe it; the tests cover the refusal, the identity, a discharge not started, an unknown admission, the clearance and its reconciliation, and the PHI log.

Confirmed: a queue-only Prescription queue is intended. Pharmacy Admin holds pharmacy.queue.view for one purpose, the supervisor watching the counter's pending queue (no screen of its own uses it), without prescription.view or pharmacy.dispense. The pharmacy_admin workspace now also_uses rx_queue: GET /meta/handbook (unscoped and ?workspace=pharmacy_admin) lists rx_queue inside Pharmacy Admin, workspace still naming its home (pharmacy), page screens/rx_queue, with one task for that role: GET /prescriptions/pending. GET /prescriptions/{prescription_id} stays FORBIDDEN without prescription.view and no permission changed. The realtime events pharmacy.prescription.pending and medication.order.updated already reach the role (audience pharmacy.queue.view), so the queue refreshes as at the counter. Offer it read-only: a row opens nothing and there is no dispense action unless the user's tasks contain them (a user who also holds the Pharmacist role works in Pharmacy Counter). The cause was the one of #21: the bundle's roles.partial, which now comes with roles.page_for (the roles whose handbook lists the screen; get_roles(role) adds pages): see that answer. From fixed_in on (compare overview's server_build with fixed_in): refresh GET /meta/workspaces and GET /meta/handbook?workspace=pharmacy_admin, re-read get_screen_bundle('rx_queue') (pharmacy_admin is in roles.page_for), add the queue to Pharmacy Admin's navigation with its F1 page for that one task and the FAQ entry, and re-read get_ui_quality_brief(workspace='pharmacy_admin') (frontend guide 17's Pharmacy Admin section adds a read). The playbook clinical-and-prescriptions (Dispensing) and guide 12 describe the queue-only journey. The screen's rules and endpoints are unchanged, so no checklist item moves.

Confirmed, and you handled it the right way (no help page invented). The bundle's roles.partial only meant that the doctors may call some of Patient search's endpoints (the search, the profile and the dues summary, never PATCH /patients/{patient_id}, which needs patient.update), while GET /meta/handbook lists another workspace's screen only when the user may call all of it, or when one of the user's workspaces names it in also_uses, and the Doctor workspace did not. The doctors hold patient.search and patient.view for this, so it does now: GET /meta/workspaces shows doctor also_uses ["patient_search"], and GET /meta/handbook (unscoped and ?workspace=doctor) lists patient_search inside the Doctor workspace, workspace still naming its home (reception), page screens/patient_search, with only the tasks the user may perform: for the Doctor role GET /patients/search, GET /patients/{patient_id} and GET /patients/{patient_id}/financial-summary, never the edit. Clinical Specialists and Surgeons (the Doctor workspace too) get it the same way; workspace=reception stays FORBIDDEN and no permission changed. The root of this report and #22 was the bundle itself: roles.partial names every role that may make one call of a screen (2,261 role and screen pairs, mostly a shared lookup such as the patient search), which reads like a menu entry. The bundle's roles section now also has page_for: the roles whose GET /meta/handbook lists the screen (the same rule, for a user with that one role and every service Active; a test compares the two), and get_roles(role) adds pages. A partial role outside page_for (the pharmacist or a nurse on Patient search, for instance) makes those calls from its own screens: never offer it that screen. Keep building the menu from the logged-in user's GET /meta/handbook, as you do. The workspace review follows the same rule: its write list leaves out the writes of a linked screen that no role of the workspace may make, so the doctor's review asks for no profile edit (and the Owner's none of collecting cash on Receivables). From fixed_in on (compare overview's server_build with fixed_in): re-read get_screen_bundle('patient_search') (roles.page_for), keep Patient search in the doctor's navigation read-only (no edit control, as its tasks say), write its F1 page for the doctor's tasks and the doctor's FAQ entry, re-read get_ui_quality_brief(workspace='doctor') (frontend guide 17's doctor section adds a read: find the patient registered in the review and open the profile, with its F1 page), and rerun your phase-2 screen smoke test. Guides 10 and 12 explain page_for. The screen's rules and endpoints are unchanged, so no checklist item moves.

Thank you for reconciling by reading instead of repeating the writes, and for the receipts. We could not establish the root cause and do not claim that every network break is gone: the Windows event log of the DEV server shows no restart of the MCP service between 22:04 UTC on 24 October and 08:43 UTC on 25 October (your session was not lost to a restart), and sandbox_call returns the API's answer, or its own error, as a tool result, never by dropping the connection. 'Transport closed' is what an MCP client reports when the connection, its session or the answer's event stream breaks between it and the server, whatever the tool did. What the server had was the most fragile transport the protocol allows: a stateful session kept in the MCP process's memory (reaped after 30 idle minutes) and every answer sent as an event stream through the TLS gateway, which also compresses it, and your VPN. From fixed_in on (compare overview's server_build with fixed_in): (1) the MCP server is stateless with plain JSON answers: each tool call is one HTTP request and its answer, with no session id to lose and no stream held open (no tool needed either). Your agent needs no change; reconnect it once after the upgrade (a new agent session). (2) sandbox_status returns recent_calls: your implementation's last 20 sandbox_call outcomes, newest first (method, path, as_user, idempotency_key, outcome, status, request_id, idempotent_replay, ms, error_type), kept per developer and implementation in the MCP service's memory (a restart empties it). outcome is answered (with the API's status and request_id), refused or failed (stopped before sending), not_sent (no connection: the API never saw the request), uncertain (sent, and the API's answer never reached the MCP server) or 'no answer recorded' (still running, or the tool call itself was cut off). A key the sandbox generates is recorded before the request is sent, so you see it in every case. (3) When the answer is lost between the MCP server and the API, sandbox_call itself answers outcome uncertain or not_sent with error_type, the elapsed ms and the original idempotency_key, instead of a bare error. Nothing is ever retried. After a transport error, read recent_calls first: answered gives you the lost answer; after uncertain or 'no answer recorded', re-read the record and follow the endpoint's write_semantics, and repeat a write only with the same idempotency_key and payload on an endpoint that takes one, exactly as you did by hand. Frontend guide 10 (the sandbox section and the tool table) says this. If an answer is lost again, report the UTC time, server_build, method and path and the recent_calls entry: it tells us whether the API answered, and we will read the gateway's and the MCP service's logs for that minute.
